purpose: Independent practice of D2.1 — using impossible / possible / certain. Used as Lesson 1 consolidation artifact.
student_learning_goal: I can name events as impossible, possible, or certain.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can name events as impossible, possible, or certain.
header.character_watermark: Lucky Lou the Loon in the top-right corner with a magnifying glass. Small (~1.5in tall). References blueprint.recurring_characters.

parts.part_title: Part 1: Circle I, P, or C.
parts.student_instructions: Read each event. Circle I (impossible), P (possible), or C (certain).
parts.visual_layout: Six event rows stacked vertically. Each row has the event text on the left and three letter circles I / P / C on the right for the child to circle. Events: (1) A pig will fly today. (2) The sun will rise tomorrow. (3) It will rain at recess. (4) I will turn 100 today. (5) I will hear my name today. (6) Maple leaves will grow on a hockey stick.

image_placeholders.description: Six event rows stacked vertically for a Grade 1 worksheet, B&W line art. Each row ~5in × 0.8in. Row layout: event text on the left (~3.5in), three letter circles I / P / C on the right (~1.5in). Each circle ~0.4in in diameter, generously spaced. Events listed cover the I/P/C range with Canadian context.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P1_EVENTS at Part 1: instructions ask the child to circle I, P, or C. Keywords name the three likelihood categories.

parts.student_instructions: Look at 6 events. Write each one in the right column: IMPOSSIBLE, POSSIBLE, or CERTAIN.
parts.visual_layout: A 3-column sort table. Columns: IMPOSSIBLE, POSSIBLE, CERTAIN. Below the table, a small list of 6 events for the child to sort. Events: rain in spring, snow in summer, lunch today, see a dragon, smile from a friend, day will end.

image_placeholders.description: A 3-column sort table for a Grade 1 worksheet. Columns labelled 'IMPOSSIBLE', 'POSSIBLE', 'CERTAIN', each ~2in wide and ~3in tall, with thin solid borders. Below the table, a small list of 6 short events (each ~0.4in tall) the child reads and writes into the appropriate column.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P2_TABLE at Part 2: instructions ask the child to sort events into 3 columns. Keywords name the column headings.

parts.answer_key: IMPOSSIBLE: snow in summer, see a dragon. POSSIBLE: rain in spring, smile from a friend. CERTAIN: lunch today, day will end.

parts.student_instructions: Write ONE event for each likelihood. Make sure each event fits.

image_placeholders.description: Three labelled writing lines stacked vertically for a Grade 1 worksheet. Each line ~5in long with the label printed on the left: 'IMPOSSIBLE: ___', 'POSSIBLE: ___', 'CERTAIN: ___'. Generous height between lines.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS01_P3_LINES at Part 3: instructions ask the child to write 3 events. Keywords name the labels for each line.

parts.answer_key: Any 3 events that correctly fit each likelihood. Common: 'IMPOSSIBLE: pigs fly. POSSIBLE: rain. CERTAIN: school ends.'

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, draw something IMPOSSIBLE that would be funny if it happened.
teacher_notes: Lesson 1 consolidation artifact. Use Part 1 as the primary diagnostic signal. Children who can't distinguish I from P need the 'reality check' re-loop.
